label: lem:cauchy_grid_representation
title: Grid-contour Cauchy representation
statement:
Let \(K \subset U \subset \C\), with \(K\) compact and \(U\) open, and let
    \(f : \C \to \C\) be holomorphic on \(U\). Then there exists a finite oriented
    piecewise-linear contour \(\Gamma \subset U \setminus K\), encoded as a finite
    sequence of oriented line segments \([A_i, B_i]\) whose images lie in
    \(U \setminus K\), such that Cauchy's integral formula
    \[
      f(z) = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\sum_{i} \int_{A_i \to B_i}
        \frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta
    \]
    holds for every \(z \in K\).
proof:
By \cref{lem:compact_subset_open_collar}, fix a positive collar \(\rho>0\)
    such that the \(2\rho\)-thickening of \(K\) lies in \(U\). Cover \(K\) by a
    finite grid of axis-parallel closed squares of side \(h\) with
    \(h\sqrt 2 < \rho\); the chosen squares have closures inside \(U\). Form
    \(\Gamma\) as the algebraic boundary of the union of these squares, with
    interior edges cancelling because each appears in two adjacent squares with
    opposite orientation. Each remaining oriented edge lies in the
    \(\rho\)-thickening but outside \(K\), so \(\Gamma \subset U \setminus K\).
    For \(z \in K\), Cauchy's integral formula on \(\Gamma\) follows by
    deforming a small circle around \(z\) to the outer grid boundary via
    Cauchy-Goursat applied piecewise on the interior squares.
